title: The Missing Sunrise Violin
summary: It is Friday night at Maple Grove School. Tonight is Concert Night. At 7:10 PM, music teacher Mr. Arun Patel goes to the music room to pick up his famous violin, the Sunrise Violin. The glass case is open. The violin is gone.
crimeFacts: The violin was made in 1904 and is worth about $60,000.
Mr. Patel locked it in the glass case at 6:30 PM. Then he went to the stage to warm up the student orchestra.
He was going to play it at 7:30 PM.
The case is not broken. The violin's black travel case was left on the shelf.

victim.name: Mr. Arun Patel
victim.details: He has taught music at Maple Grove for 25 years. He is strict but kind. The Sunrise Violin was a gift from his own teacher, who has passed away. For him, it is worth much more than money. He was on stage with 30 students from 6:35 to 7:10, so he is not a suspect. His own key stayed in his pocket all night.

suspects.name: Lena Cruz
suspects.background: Lena plays violin and dreams of music college. Every afternoon she helps Mr. Patel by cleaning the music room, including the glass case. She loves her purple wool concert sweater.
suspects.evidence: Her fingerprints are all over the glass case. Her notebook says: 'Someday I'll own a violin like that.'
suspects.motive: Her family cannot pay for music college. The violin could change that.
suspects.alibi: I was doing a sound check on stage from about 6:45 to 7:00.

suspects.name: Victor Hale
suspects.background: Victor runs a violin shop in the city. He always wears a navy suit. He asked to buy the Sunrise Violin three times, and Mr. Patel said no every time.
suspects.evidence: His business card was found on the piano in the music room. Mr. Patel says Victor visited at about 6:15 and left after ten minutes.
suspects.motive: He offered $50,000. The violin could sell for much more.
suspects.alibi: I was in the parking lot, on a phone call by my car, from about 6:40 to 7:05.

suspects.name: Marcus Bell
suspects.background: Marcus has worked at the school for 10 years. He is quiet and works hard. He wears gray cotton overalls and gray work gloves. He cleans the music room at 5:30 every day.
suspects.evidence: A gray work glove was found under the piano. He also has the code to the music office key box.
suspects.motive: Last month Mr. Patel reported him for leaving the music room dirty. Marcus almost lost his job.
suspects.alibi: I was fixing the broken side-gate light with Coach Reyes, from about 6:45 to 7:05.

suspects.name: Dana Wu
suspects.background: Dana teaches cello and organized Concert Night. She wears a purple wool scarf every single day. Her family's music shop closed this spring.
suspects.evidence: A big box of extra programs sat beside her front desk all evening.
suspects.motive: Money is tight since the shop closed. She told a friend she was 'running out of options.'
suspects.alibi: I was at the front desk handing out programs the whole time, from 6:30 to 7:10. Two parents remember seeing me there, one at about 6:45 and one at about 7:00.

starterClues.title: The Door Sensor
starterClues.text: The music room door has a sensor that saves the times it opens and closes. It opened at 6:30 (Mr. Patel leaving). It opened at 6:52 and closed at 6:54. It opened again at 7:10 (Mr. Patel coming back). So the thief was inside for only about two minutes.

starterClues.title: The Lock
starterClues.text: The glass case has no scratches and no damage. It was opened with a real key. Only the violin was taken, and its travel case was left behind.

quizClues.title: The Key Box
quizClues.text: Mr. Patel's key stayed in his pocket all night, and 30 students saw him on stage. But a spare key was kept in the music office key box, and now it is missing. Only four people know the box code: Mr. Patel, Lena, Marcus, and Dana.

quizClues.title: The Purple Thread
quizClues.text: A short purple thread was caught on the metal latch of the case. A lab test says it is wool, not cotton or polyester.

quizClues.title: The Sound Booth Recording
quizClues.text: The sound tech recorded the whole sound check. From 6:48 to 6:58, Lena can be heard playing her violin without stopping. The tech watched her play and says she never left the stage.

quizClues.title: The Parking Lot Camera
quizClues.text: A camera in the far parking lot shows Victor standing next to his silver car, talking on his phone, from 6:41 to 7:03. The lot is on the other side of the school, a five-minute walk from the music room.

quizClues.title: The Work Order
quizClues.text: Coach Reyes signed a work order for the side-gate light. It says Marcus worked on it with him from 6:45 to 7:05.

quizClues.title: The Front Desk Sheet
quizClues.text: Guests sign in at the front desk. The sheet shows a gap: the last name was written at 6:49, and the next at 6:58. Sam, a 12-year-old volunteer, says that around 6:50 someone told the waiting guests, 'Back in a minute.' Also, a parent who saw Dana at 7:00 says: 'It was the first time I ever saw her without her purple scarf.'

explanation: Clue s1: The theft happened between 6:52 and 6:54.

Clues s2 and c3: The thief used a key, so it was the spare key. Only Mr. Patel, Lena, Marcus, and Dana know the code. Mr. Patel was on stage with 30 witnesses. Victor does not know the code, so he is out.
Clue c4: The thread is purple wool. Marcus wears gray cotton. Victor wears a navy suit. Among the suspects, only Lena (purple sweater) and Dana (purple scarf) wear purple wool.
Clue c5: At 6:52, Lena was on a recording playing her violin on stage. She could not be in the music room. Lena is out.
Clue c6: Victor was in the far parking lot on camera. This double-checks that he is out.
Clue c7: Marcus was fixing the side-gate light with Coach Reyes. This double-checks that he is out.

Clue c8: Dana said she never left the desk. But the sign-in sheet has a gap from 6:49 to 6:58, and Sam heard someone say 'Back in a minute.' The gap covers the exact time of the theft. At 7:00 Dana had no scarf. That matches the purple wool thread on the latch.
solution.howItHappened: Dana left the desk at 6:49. She used the box code to take the spare key. At 6:52 she opened the case, took the violin, and wrapped it in her purple scarf. The scarf snagged a thread on the latch. She left at 6:54 and hid the violin under the programs in the box beside her desk. By 6:58 she was back at the desk. She did it because of her money trouble. When the police check the program box, they find the Sunrise Violin at the bottom, wrapped in the purple scarf.

redHerrings.why: She cleans the glass every day, so her fingerprints are normal. Wishing for a violin is not stealing one. Her recorded alibi proves she was on stage.
He left his card during his 6:15 visit. Mr. Patel locked the violin in the case at 6:30, after Victor left. The camera shows Victor in the parking lot, and he does not know the key box code.
He cleans the music room at 5:30 every day, so he could have dropped the glove then. The thread is wool, but he wears cotton. His work order shows he was at the side gate.
